children: Crude oil futures fell by their biggest one-day percentage decline since July, as the market gave credence to the latest diplomatic moves aimed at bringing the U.S. and Iran to the negotiating table as well as President Trump's willingness to allow more time after the midterm elections for a diplomatic solution to end the war.

Trump's apparent shift in position "appears to be gaining credibility with investors, prompting traders to increase short positions and driving a sharp reversal in technical indicators," Peter Cardillo of Spartan Capital said in a note.

Iran's President Pezeshkian said his country’s supreme leader had allowed the government certain powers to "try to resolve the problem with dialogue," without elaborating, according to state-run news agency IRNA.
Qatari mediators reportedly traveled to Tehran on Monday night for talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Araqchi on a potential U.S.-Iran deal.

"The oil market is ‌still ⁠reacting with extreme sensitivity to every headline out of the Middle East," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo wrote. "While fears of an imminent escalation pushed prices up last week, they have dropped sharply at the start of this week as diplomatic talks between the U.S. and Iran continue."

"Today’s selling appeared to be much accentuated by what has become an overbought technical condition following last month’s sizable crude price gains that saw Brent advance by more than 13%," Ritterbusch & Associates wrote, adding the nearly 10% decline at one point during the session looks like "a significant overreaction to today’s headlines."
Meanwhile, the Trump administration is pushing to restore Russian natural gas sales to Europe via pipelines running through Ukraine, as
reported that the idea is part of negotiations to secure an energy ceasefire ahead of the winter.

The plan reportedly would include selling Russian gas via a U.S. intermediary to circumvent European sanctions, which could create a lucrative opportunity for investors; Europe has been phasing out the purchase of Russian gas, aiming to completely end it by 2027.
